content: CORS: the port is part of the origin, so Vite's default http://localhost:5173 calling an Express API on http://localhost:8080 is cross-origin, and http://localhost:5173 vs http://127.0.0.1:5173 are different origins too. curl and Postman ignore CORS entirely, so 'it works in Postman' is a false negative signal. Two fixes: allow the exact dev origin on the API (cors({origin: ['http://localhost:5173', 'https://admin.example.com']}), no trailing slash, exact scheme+host+port) or proxy /api through the Vite dev server (server.proxy in vite.config.js, then call relative URLs). For a credentialed setup the API must echo the exact origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true - a wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials is rejected by the browser, which is the classic 'works locally, broken on deploy' failure (Netlify + Render case: the header came back as * despite an explicit origin list, so the credentials check failed). Register cors() before routes and before error handlers, and remember app.options('*', cors()) if it is applied per route. What does not work: mode:'no-cors' (opaque response), disabling browser security, adding the header to the request instead of the response. Critically, CORS is not access control - it does not stop curl/Postman/server-to-server calls, so the API must still enforce auth and role checks itself. JWT storage in Flutter: flutter_secure_storage is the mobile choice (Keychain on iOS/macOS, Android KeyStore + encrypted storage on Android) and shared_preferences / NSUserDefaults is explicitly documented as unsuitable for secrets - plaintext on disk, trivially readable from an unencrypted backup or a jailbroken device. flutter_secure_storage v10 defaults to RSA OAEP + AES-GCM on Android and requires minSdkVersion 23; it needs allowBackup=false or a backup exclusion in AndroidManifest or restored devices throw java.security.InvalidKeyException: Failed to unwrap key; on iOS use KeychainAccessibility.first_unlock_this_device for auth tokens so they are not carried into a new device's backup. flutter_secure_storage does not work on Flutter Web (there, httpOnly cookies plus a separate CSRF token is the pattern). Secure storage is for secrets only - cached floor plans and graph JSON should live in normal storage; it is also too slow to read per frame.
